questions.q: Why polish a single chart for the presentation instead of showing the two-panel exploration figure?
options: Two-panel charts are not allowed in presentations
The exploration figure was for us; the audience needs one message with a finding title, a highlight, and a baseline
Single charts always contain more data
Because matplotlib cannot draw two panels
questions.explain: Presentations carry one message per chart. Exploration figures are working tools for the analyst.

questions.q: What does the dashed horizontal line at 19.6% add to the polished chart?
options: It shows the maximum churn
It marks the overall baseline so each bar can be judged against it
It proves causation
It removes the need for a title
questions.explain: A baseline gives context: a bar means more when you can see it against the overall rate.

questions.q: In the four-part presentation, where does 'tickets may be a symptom of an unhappy customer' belong?
options: The answer
The ask
The evidence
The caveat
questions.explain: It qualifies the finding: the data shows an association, not a cause.

questions.q: Which is the best 'ask' given the analysis?
options: A two-month pilot with proactive outreach at the third ticket and a comparison group
Cut all support tickets by force
Deploy a predictive model immediately
Ignore the first-year customers
questions.explain: A pilot with a comparison group lets the team measure whether outreach reduces churn, testing more than an association.

questions.q: Which item belongs in a portfolio 'data note' for a generated dataset?
options: A claim that it came from a real company
Nothing; data notes are unnecessary
Only the chart colors
A plain statement that the data is generated, plus the columns and known issues
questions.explain: Be candid about provenance. Describe columns and known issues, and say plainly if the data is generated.
